solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Significant curtailment of University course

indicators.note: curtailing means cutting short, so the final letter of the course name is chopped off

parts.note: Greats is the Oxford University course in classics

explanation.surface: Something important about a university cutting its course short.
explanation.walkthrough: GREATS, the Oxford honours course in classics and philosophy, loses its last letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a significant event is a great one, of large importance.

clue.text: Detective in Georgia unwise to burst in uninvited

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
tec is short for detective
rash means unwise

explanation.surface: A rash detective in Georgia barges in without invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to enter a party or event without being invited.

clue.text: Detective encouraged in case?

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
up means in good spirits, encouraged

explanation.surface: A detective feels heartened during a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like the detective's investigation, but it is a verb: to case a place is to look it over.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye up is to look over carefully, much as a burglar cases a house.

clue.text: Heart's latest stirrings provided by lingerie items

indicators.note: latest means the final letter of heart

parts.note: eddies are swirling movements in water or air

explanation.surface: The heart flutters at the sight of some underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy is a one-piece undergarment combining camisole and knickers.

clue.text: One scoundrel coming back in to jeer American — that's marvellous

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed in the middle of the jeering word

parts.note: to boo is to jeer

indicators.note: coming back means the words one and scoundrel are read in reverse

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain returns to be booed by an American, who finds it wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns the scoundrel and one into DACI, which 'in' places inside the jeer. Bodacious is American slang, hence the US flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodacious is American slang for excellent or remarkable, hence marvellous.

clue.text: French island in sea inlet? Bridge designer required

indicators.note: in means the island word sits inside the inlet word

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea
ile is French for island

explanation.surface: An island in a bay needs someone to design a bridge to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Donald Bailey designed the portable Bailey bridge used in the Second World War.

clue.text: Food shop I established in spirit and excitement

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

indicators.note: established in means set inside, so the I goes into the spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A delicatessen I set up deals in spirits and thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium can mean wild excitement or ecstasy, as well as a disturbed mental state.

clue.text: Conservative enthusiastically supporting demand

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed beneath, so the enthusiasm comes after

parts.note: all for means enthusiastically in favour

explanation.surface: A Tory eagerly backs a demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To call for something is to demand or require it.

clue.text: Superior officer and copper incline to apprehend tenor, one behaving mysteriously

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize, so the lean word holds the tenor letter

parts.note: a ship's list is an incline

explanation.surface: A senior officer and a policeman tilt toward arresting a tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the element, CU.
explanation.definitionFit: An occultist practises magic and the occult, so deals in mysteries.

clue.text: Germ brought about onset of pandemic with alacrity

indicators.note: brought about means taken around, so the germ word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a seed is a germ, the starting point of growth

indicators.note: onset of means the first letter of pandemic

explanation.surface: A germ quickly started a pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: alacrity is eager speed or briskness.

clue.text: Pore over millions invested in work on farm — it's a routine operation

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the reading and the millions go within the farm work

parts.note: to till is to work the soil on a farm
to pore over a text is to read it

explanation.surface: Studying how millions are spent on agricultural work is a dull routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a treadmill is a tedious, unvarying round of work.

clue.text: A lot of good fortune about, leading to wealth

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter of the fortune word is dropped

parts.note: luck is good fortune
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Plenty of good luck around leads to riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or profit, often with a hint of disapproval; a synonym for wealth.

clue.text: Sudden idea to cover grain

parts.note: a cap is a cover, as on a bottle
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly thinks of covering some grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim, a sudden unaccountable change of mind or impulse.

clue.text: Upset, started new round after trump

indicators.note: after places the leading piece behind the trump word

parts.note: in card games to ruff is to trump
in cards, to lead is to play first in a new trick, so led means started one

explanation.surface: A card player gets annoyed after playing a trump and starting the next round.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from card play (bridge, whist): RUFF is to play a trump, and LED is to have played the first card of a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone ruffled is flustered or upset.

clue.text: Approach shown by skilled players, doubling clubs and spades

indicators.note: doubling means a second clubs letter and a second spades letter are added beside the ones already in the word

parts.note: aces are expert players
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
S is the abbreviation for spades in cards

explanation.surface: A card-table approach by expert players who double in clubs and spades.
explanation.walkthrough: ACES already holds one C and one S; 'doubling' adds a second of each, giving ACCESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: access is a means of approach or entry to a place.

clue.text: Vocal couple at front of class engaged in canoodling

indicators.note: a couple is two, so the first two letters of class are taken

parts.note: canoodling couples are amorous

explanation.surface: Two pupils at the front of the class are noisily cuddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamorous means loud and insistent, so vocal in protest.

clue.text: Argue vaguely about introduction of colour in revolutionary painting

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other pieces
vaguely signals the letters of argue are loosely rearranged
revolutionary means turned round, so the word in is read backwards
introduction of means the first letter of colour

explanation.surface: People argue vaguely about colour in a revolutionary painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaguely' makes GUERA; 'revolutionary' makes NI. 'revolutionary' seems to describe the painting, but it only turns one small word.
explanation.definitionFit: Guernica is Picasso's 1937 painting of the bombing of the Basque town.

clue.text: Creature with wings, one on right having difference over left

parts.note: a means one
a change is a difference

explanation.surface: A winged creature on the right differs from the one on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: An archangel is an angel of high rank, traditionally depicted with wings.

clue.text: Extended journey — miles over a desert (hot interior)

indicators.note: interior means put inside, so the hot letter goes within the desert phrase

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert them
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A long trek of miles across a hot desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a sandy place but is a verb: to rat on is to betray or abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long race, or by extension any long and demanding undertaking.

clue.text: Wielder of axe named ash for demolition

indicators.note: demolition knocks things apart, so the letters of these two words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An ash tree has been earmarked to be cut down by someone with an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A headsman was an executioner who beheaded the condemned with an axe.

clue.text: Homes erected to house a European or Asiatic?

indicators.note: to house means to contain, so the reversed homes hold the letter a
in a down clue erected means built upwards, so the word for homes is reversed

parts.note: semis are semi-detached houses

explanation.surface: Houses are built for a European or someone from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: SEMIS, British for semi-detached houses, reversed is SIMES; A goes inside, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Siamese means from Siam, the old name for Thailand, so Asian; the question mark flags the loose sense.

clue.text: Everyone initially restricted by constant source of irritation, recalled in a fever

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole assembled string is read in reverse

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: restricted by means held inside the irritation word

parts.note: an itch is a source of irritation

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of everyone

explanation.surface: An irritating itch that keeps coming back leaves everyone feverish.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside ITCH to make ITCEH; after C that gives CITCEH, which 'recalled' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic once meant feverish, as in a hectic flush, before its modern sense of frantic.

clue.text: Stuff on prescription that will have you looking better

definitions.text: Stuff on prescription that will have you looking better

parts.words: Stuff on prescription that will have you looking better
parts.note: reads like a medicine improving your appearance, but means glasses that improve your vision

explanation.surface: Medication that will make you look healthier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking better' seems to mean appearing healthier, but it means seeing more clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles and contact lenses are prescribed by an optician to correct vision.

clue.text: Mostly stiff and tense in arrangement

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the stiff word

parts.note: formal means stiff in manner
T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar

explanation.surface: Being mostly rigid and tense in how things are laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: A format is the layout or arrangement of something, such as a page or programme.

clue.text: First to oust this person, American getting cheers, relatively speaking?

indicators.note: to oust is to push out, so the personal letter is expelled from the word for first

parts.note: prior means first or earlier
the setter speaking of themself is I
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Pushing out the first person, an American gets applause, comparatively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIOR loses I to give PROR. Ta and cheers are both everyday British ways of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro rata means in proportion, so it describes things measured relative to one another.

clue.text: Head to North after coming round in rising alarm

indicators.note: coming round means surrounding, so the reversed head word encloses the other piece
in a down clue going to the north means reading upwards, so the head word is written backwards

parts.note: a cap is worn on the head, and to cap is to top or head something

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read upwards, so the word in is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone heads north after recovering consciousness, amid growing alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to North' turns CAP into PAC and 'rising' turns IN into NI; 'coming round' puts NI inside PAC. 'rising alarm' wants to be the definition; 'rising' is needed for the second reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, a synonym for alarm.

clue.text: A popular firm making a return having covered each part of the globe

indicators.note: having covered means the reversed string surrounds the each abbreviation
making a return means the words a, popular and firm are read backwards

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A popular company comes back after covering every part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a return' gives OCNIA, which 'having covered' wraps round the abbreviation for each.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the region taking in Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands.

clue.text: Is on trail of number (unknown) engaging in racket

indicators.note: on the trail of means coming behind, so is follows the number

parts.note: in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Someone tracks an unidentified number running a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests a criminal scheme, but here it means din.
explanation.definitionFit: Being noisy means making a racket, a loud din.

clue.text: Move cautiously around old snare

indicators.note: around means the move word wraps round the abbreviation for old

parts.note: to nose is to edge forward carefully

explanation.surface: Someone creeps carefully round an old trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a noose is a loop that tightens, used as a snare to catch animals.

clue.text: Hurrying to protect Frenchwoman in onslaught

indicators.note: to protect means to surround, so the hurrying word encloses the Frenchwoman

parts.note: haring means running fast like a hare
Mme is the abbreviation for Madame, a Frenchwoman

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to shield a Frenchwoman during an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammering is a heavy beating or defeat, so a sustained onslaught.

clue.text: Fruit lolly we returned with fruitcake

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money, cash

indicators.note: returned means the word we is read backwards

parts.note: a fruitcake is slang for an eccentric, a nut

explanation.surface: An ice lolly and fruitcake are brought back as a fruity treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for money as well as an ice lolly on a stick, and fruitcake is slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the cashew nut is a fruit, the seed of the cashew apple.

clue.text: Offering allegiance (after initial change of side) for monarch

indicators.note: the first letter switches side from left to right, so L becomes R

parts.note: loyal means showing allegiance

explanation.surface: A subject pledges loyalty to the king after switching sides.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R are the usual abbreviations for left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal as a noun is a member of a royal family, here standing for the monarch.
